paper_title: Bithienopyrroledione-Based Copolymers, Versatile Semiconductors for Balanced Ambipolar Thin-Film Transistors and Organic Solar Cells with Voc > 1 V

qa_pairs.question: What structural characteristics of bithienopyrroledione (bi-TPD) make it a promising building block for ambipolar polymer semiconductors?
qa_pairs.answer: Bithienopyrroledione (bi-TPD) is a planar derivative of thieno[3,4-c]pyrrole-4,6-dione (TPD) that possesses a planar structure and exhibits stronger electron-withdrawing properties than TPD, which facilitates its use in high-performance ambipolar materials.
qa_pairs.source_title: Bithienopyrroledione-Based Copolymers, Versatile Semiconductors for Balanced Ambipolar Thin-Film Transistors and Organic Solar Cells with Voc > 1 V

qa_pairs.question: What are the maximum electron and hole mobilities achieved by P1-based thin-film transistors, and under what processing conditions?
qa_pairs.answer: P1-based thin-film transistors achieve a high electron mobility of 1.02 cm²/V·s and a hole mobility of 0.33 cm²/V·s when the films are thermally annealed at 160°C.
qa_pairs.source_title: Bithienopyrroledione-Based Copolymers, Versatile Semiconductors for Balanced Ambipolar Thin-Film Transistors and Organic Solar Cells with Voc > 1 V

qa_pairs.question: How does the power conversion efficiency (PCE) and open-circuit voltage (Voc) of a P1:PC71BM organic solar cell compare when processed without additives or post-treatments?
qa_pairs.answer: Without any additives or post-treatments, the P1:PC71BM-based device achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 6.46% and a high open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 1.02 V.
qa_pairs.source_title: Bithienopyrroledione-Based Copolymers, Versatile Semiconductors for Balanced Ambipolar Thin-Film Transistors and Organic Solar Cells with Voc > 1 V

qa_pairs.question: Explain the relationship between the HOMO energy levels of P1 and P2 and the open-circuit voltage (Voc) observed in their respective organic solar cells.
qa_pairs.answer: The high open-circuit voltage (Voc > 1.0 V) in P1 and P2-based solar cells is primarily attributed to the low-lying HOMO energy levels of the polymers, which are -5.72 eV for P1 and -5.85 eV for P2. A deeper HOMO level generally correlates with a higher Voc in organic solar cells when paired with a specific acceptor like PC71BM.
qa_pairs.source_title: Bithienopyrroledione-Based Copolymers, Versatile Semiconductors for Balanced Ambipolar Thin-Film Transistors and Organic Solar Cells with Voc > 1 V

qa_pairs.question: What is the effect of replacing benzothiadiazole (BT) with 5,6-difluorobenzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole (2FBT) on the electronic energy levels of the resulting polymer P2?
qa_pairs.answer: Replacing BT with 2FBT deepens both the HOMO and LUMO energy levels of the polymer (P2). This is due to the stronger electron-withdrawing nature of the fluorine atoms in the 2FBT unit compared to the unsubstituted BT unit.
qa_pairs.source_title: Bithienopyrroledione-Based Copolymers, Versatile Semiconductors for Balanced Ambipolar Thin-Film Transistors and Organic Solar Cells with Voc > 1 V

qa_pairs.question: Compare the sensitivity of P1 and P2 thin-film transistors to thermal annealing in terms of charge carrier mobility.
qa_pairs.answer: P1 is highly sensitive to thermal annealing; at 160°C, its electron mobility increases significantly by 1-2 orders of magnitude. In contrast, the transistor performance of P2 films is nearly independent of the thermal annealing temperature.
qa_pairs.source_title: Bithienopyrroledione-Based Copolymers, Versatile Semiconductors for Balanced Ambipolar Thin-Film Transistors and Organic Solar Cells with Voc > 1 V

qa_pairs.question: Based on GIXD analysis, how does the molecular orientation of P1 films annealed at 160°C facilitate charge transport?
qa_pairs.answer: P1 films annealed at 160°C exhibit a coexistence of both edge-on and face-on molecular orientations with a pi-pi stacking distance of 3.48 Å. This mixed orientation facilitates the formation of 3D charge transport pathways, which contributes to the high observed mobilities.
qa_pairs.source_title: Bithienopyrroledione-Based Copolymers, Versatile Semiconductors for Balanced Ambipolar Thin-Film Transistors and Organic Solar Cells with Voc > 1 V

qa_pairs.question: Why are the energy levels of P1 and P2 polymers well-suited for creating ambipolar transistors using gold (Au) electrodes?
qa_pairs.answer: Ambipolar transport is facilitated because the LUMO levels (approx. -4.0 eV) and HOMO levels (-5.7 to -5.8 eV) of P1 and P2 align well with the work function of gold (approx. 5.2 eV). This alignment minimizes the injection barriers for both holes and electrons from the Au source/drain electrodes.
qa_pairs.source_title: Bithienopyrroledione-Based Copolymers, Versatile Semiconductors for Balanced Ambipolar Thin-Film Transistors and Organic Solar Cells with Voc > 1 V
